chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Isma'il ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'An obligatory salat is better than twenty Hajj; and a Hajj is better than a house filled with gold given in charity until it is depleted.'

key_terms.حَجَّةً: A single Hajj pilgrimage — the annual pilgrimage to Mecca, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ فَرِيضَةٌ: An obligatory prayer (salat farida) — one of the five daily prayers that every Muslim is required to perform
key_terms.يُتَصَدَّقُ: Given in charity (sadaqa) — voluntary charitable giving, distinct from the obligatory zakat

ai.seo_question: What is the merit of obligatory prayer (salat) compared to Hajj and charity according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a hierarchy of worship by declaring that a single obligatory prayer surpasses twenty Hajj pilgrimages, and that one Hajj surpasses giving away a house full of gold in charity until it is entirely depleted. This teaching emphasizes that consistent ritual obligations like salat hold supreme spiritual merit. The Imam spoke in a context where the community needed clarity on which acts of worship were most valued, reinforcing that daily obligatory prayer is the cornerstone of Islamic practice.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Ismai l Bin ammar, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The Salāt is an Obligation, being better than twenty Hajj; and a Hajj is better than a house filled with gold given in charity until it depletes’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by af-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from Isma’if ibn ‘Ammar from abu Basir who has said the following: “

Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’Performing an obligatory Salah (prayer) is more virtuous than performing one Hajj. Performing one Hajj is more virtuous than giving in charity one whole house full of gold.’”
